prompt: What does a black-box tester compare?

choices.text: What it does with what it should do
choices.why: Right: from inputs and outputs, against the specification.

choices.text: The code with the specification, line by line, before running anything at all
choices.why: That needs the code, which black box does not read.

choices.text: Two versions of the code
choices.why: Black box sees no code.

choices.text: How long the program takes on each input
choices.why: Timing can be observed from outside, but it is not the definition.

prompt: Why does a black-box test of `tickets.py` survive Rafael rewriting it from scratch?

choices.text: Black-box tests never fail
choices.why: They fail whenever behaviour departs from the rule.

choices.text: Because it tests each line of the code exactly once
choices.why: That is a white-box idea, and lines change in a rewrite.

choices.text: Python keeps old tests
choices.why: Nothing of the sort.

choices.text: It was written against the rule, and the rule did not change
choices.why: Right: tests against code structure may have to be rewritten with it.

prompt: Suppose `tickets.py` secretly gave a discount on one particular date. Why would black-box testing from Joana’s rule not find it?
hint: What points a tester at that date?

choices.text: Nothing in the rule points at that date
choices.why: Right: you only test the behaviours you thought of.

choices.text: Black box cannot run the program on a specific date
choices.why: It could, if something told the tester which one.

choices.text: Dates are a white-box concept that only the code itself can reveal to a tester
choices.why: Dates are ordinary inputs; the problem is which one to try.

choices.text: It would find it on the first run
choices.why: Only if the first run happened to use that date.

test at the edges of the groups

prompt: Why did Lia write the expected result before running each case?

choices.text: The test tool requires it
choices.why: There is no tool here; it is a habit.

choices.text: To save time

prompt: How many reais does `tickets.py` charge a student on a Wednesday evening?
hint: A quarter of the full price.

prompt: Before Joana answered, why could Lia not decide by testing whether R$ 9,00 was a defect?
hint: Where is the expected result written?

choices.text: Wednesday tests are forbidden
choices.why: Nothing forbids them.

choices.text: She needed to read the code first
choices.why: The code shows what it does, which she already knew; not what it should do.

choices.text: The expected result for that input was written nowhere
choices.why: Right: no run can say what Joana meant.

choices.text: The program crashed
choices.why: It printed a confident R$ 9,00.

prompt: What was Joana’s answer, which became the rule’s fifth sentence?

choices.text: Reductions add up
choices.why: That is the reading she rejected.

choices.text: Students pay half every day except Wednesday, when they pay full price like everybody
choices.why: On Wednesday everybody pays half.

choices.text: Wednesday discount is cancelled
choices.why: Wednesday stayed half price.

choices.text: Half price is the most any ticket is reduced
choices.why: Right: so the student on Wednesday pays R$ 18,00.

prompt: Rafael implemented exactly what was written. Where was the Wednesday defect, then?

choices.text: In Rafael’s use of the `//` operator for division
choices.why: The division is correct; applying it twice is the issue.

choices.text: In the test table
choices.why: The table found nothing wrong because it had no combinations.

choices.text: Nowhere: R$ 9,00 is the right price for a student on Wednesday
choices.why: Joana’s answer makes it R$ 18,00.

choices.text: In what the requirement did not say
choices.why: Right: two reductions, and no sentence for both at once.

prompt: Why is a crash the easiest failure to judge?

choices.text: Crashes are rare
choices.why: Rarity has nothing to do with judging.

choices.text: Tracebacks show the expected result for the input that caused them

choices.text: Customers report them politely
choices.why: Not the argument.

choices.text: No requirement has to mention it
choices.why: Right: some outcomes are wrong whatever the rule says.

choices.text: They are more common

choices.text: They take longer to run
choices.why: Speed is not the issue.

choices.text: They only happen in production

prompt: Order the steps that turned the Wednesday combination into a fixable defect.
hint: From a missing sentence to a test.
items: run a student on a Wednesday
notice the rule has no expected result for it
ask Joana, with the command that shows it
Joana answers: half is the most
the case becomes a test with an expected price
trap: The answer comes before the test, because the answer is what the test checks against.
